text.p: The French government favours an alliance between the state-controlled nuclear engineering group Framatome and engineering company Alcatel Alsthom, Industry Minister Franck Borotra said on Friday.
He told the afternoon daily Le Monde in an interview that Britain's General Electric Company Plc (GEC) could join the group later.
"The government is favourable to an eventual alliance between Framatome and Alcatel Alsthom in its energy activites, with GEC joining up afterwards," he told the newspaper.
Borotra's comments came after Framatome said on Monday a planned merger with Anglo-French joint venture GEC-Alsthom seemed unlikely.

Framatome said GEC had wanted to take a 50 percent stake in the new combination, equal to its current stake in the GEC Alsthom joint venture with Alcatel Alsthom. But this aim went against the government's stipulation that French interests keep a majority in the nuclear group.
Borotra said that he wanted Framatome to be privatised and be part of a strong group "the faster the better".
But, he stressed, the government "would not abandon its desire to keep its control of the nuclear domain".
